messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High error rates and packet loss observed on customer ACME private VPN (eu-west-1). Auto-threshold triggered. Paging on-call.

sara: @oncall-desk got the page, looking now. seeing spikes in tcp retransmits from gateway-euw1-03 to acme-vpn-02

jamal: I can confirm. BGP flaps observed on the peering session to ACME. bgp state keeps bouncing between ESTABLISHED/ACTIVE.

leo: Any regional context? AZ-wide or just the host?

sara: So far looks eu-west-1a and 1b core-facing routers. Control plane shows intermittent route withdrawals for ACME prefixes.

marta: Customer impact: ACME reports API timeouts for their internal health checks. They use the VPN for control plane traffic — likely why.

cust-acme-netops: Confirmed from our side: multiple sessions dropped, we see 20-40% packet loss to Redwood gateway within the last 30m. Working on an ops-side BGP reset now.

jamal: Sharing quick diagnostics:

```
# show bgp neighbors | include acme
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcvd MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.254.10.2     4 65020  123456  123460        0    0    0 00:04:12  Active
```

sara: traceroute from gateway-euw1-03 -> acme-vpn-02:

```
1  10.0.0.1
2  10.0.5.2
3  * * *
4  * * *
```

leo: Looks like a blackhole after our spine. Could be a flapping route causing backend to drop. Any recent infra changes in euw1?

marta: No infra deploys in the past 2h. Network config push was yesterday.

jamal: I'm going to force withdraw and re-advertise ACME prefixes from gw03 to try to re-stabilize the session.

sara: Before that, check if route-reflector is receiving updates. If RR is dropping, re-advertise won't help.

jamal: Good call. RR shows intermittent TCP reset to the neighbor. Dumping syslog.

```
Mar 15 10:07:04 bgpd[1234]: Connection from 10.254.10.2 closed by remote host (peer reset)
Mar 15 10:07:05 bgpd[1234]: BGP: 10.254.10.2 ASN 65020 Session reset
```

leo: Could be a flaky network path between us and the customer's VPN concentrator (or their edge). Ask ACME if they saw any interface errors/maintenance.

cust-acme-netops: No maintenance. We see some errors on our primary concentrator interface, investigating hardware fans/ASIC.

marta: Mitigation plan:
- Fail traffic to ACME over secondary Direct Connect/backup VPN in the same region (if available)
- Apply temporary route dampening on our side for that peer to avoid constant flaps
- Coordinate BGP reset with ACME
- Monitor customer-facing errors and rollback once stable

sara: Can we kick over to backup? Route config shows a standby tunnel via gw-euw1-07.

jamal: Initiating graceful failover now: will set local-preference lower on gw03 and advertise via gw07.

```
# aws ec2 modify-vpn-connection --vpn-connection-id vpn-abc123 --transit-options "{\"LocalPreference\": 90}"
```

sara: Done. Traffic shift started, packet loss dropping from 30% -> ~5% across flows within 2 minutes.

cust-acme-netops: Seeing improvement on our end, tests passing over standby link. Thanks.

leo: While traffic is on standby, let's collect pcap on gw03 and request ACME to capture on their concentrator. Also scheduling an on-call handoff when folks need to sleep.

marta: Capturing 60s pcap now and uploading to the secure bucket. Link: https://internal-artifacts/reports/1839504321/gw03-pcap.pcap (restricted)

jamal: After analysis, gw03 NIC showed intermittent CRC/frame errors. I'll open a ticket with cloud provider for hardware replacement. Marking gw03 as degraded.

sara: For the customer-facing incident note: impact window ~1839501000 -> 1839504200 (partial) and mitigation at 1839504380 (failover completed). Will draft and share to #support to notify ACME.

cust-acme-netops: Acknowledged. Please include the temporary mitigation and our planned handover window.

marta: On-call handoff: @leo will take next 6h rotation for post-mortem and follow-up with provider. @sara please include the pcap and bgp logs in the incident ticket.

leo: Yep I got it. I'll keep monitoring and update the postmortem draft.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity reduced to S2. Traffic restored via backup path. Provider ticket opened: CP-45218. Next update in 60m or on significant change.

sara: Quick checklist for follow-ups:
- Provider hardware replacement ETA
- ACME confirm stable on primary after replacement
- Add automated detection for BGP-reset spike patterns to avoid noisy paging
- Postmortem + RCA within 48h

marta: Adding: plan to implement route-flap dampening thresholds per-customer (trial) to reduce blast radius.

cust-acme-netops: Thanks all. We'll coordinate scheduled BGP restart with you once provider confirms hw swap.

leo: Closing the live thread. Will reopen if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
__note: This document is a synthesized Slack incident thread for Redwood Inference testing. All names and details are fictional but realistic for dataset generation.
